newsitem.title: USA: True North to buy Bozell for $440 million.
newsitem.headline: True North to buy Bozell for $440 million.

text.p: Global advertising agency True North Communications Inc, said Thursday it agreed to buy its smaller rival Bozell, Jacobs, Kenyon and Eckhardt Inc. in a transaction valued at about $440 million.

The deal, which had been expected, would create the sixth-largest advertising agency in the world, with more than $11.5 billion in billings and more than 11,000 employees in 297 offices around the world, True North said.
It said the agreement virtually doubles its size, with projected revenues of $1.2 billion.
True North, which has made more than a dozen smaller acquisitions this year, currently ranks as the world's seventh-largest advertising agency and Bozell ranks 14th.
True North's stock, which did not trade early Thursday, closed Wednesday at $23.06 a share on the New York Stock Exchange. Bozell, which is based in New York, is privately held.
As part of the deal, which was approved by both boards, True North will issue 0.51 shares of stock for each share of Bozell.
Bozell will continue to operate as an independent company, led by current chairman, Leo-Arthur Kelmenson, True North said.

Bozell's units include Poppe Tyson, which specializes in interactive digital technology; Temerlin McClain, a U.S. agency whose clients include J.C. Penney and American Airlines; Bozell Sawyer Miller Group, the eighth-largest U.S. public relations company; McCracken Brooks, a marketing communications company; and Bozell Wellness Worldwide, a network of multinational companies specializing in healthcare advertising.
True North already owns Foote, Cone & Belding Worldwide, which is the largest advertising agency in North America, with a client list that includes AT&T, Levi Strauss & Co. and Nabisco.

"With this transaction we accomplish two of the primary goals we established with the formation of True North in 1995: first, we now have multiple global advertising brands; and second, we're the clear leader in the important growth area of interactive digital technology," said Bruce Mason, True North chairman.

True North said it expects the transaction to be boost its earnings in the first full year, which will be 1998. The company said it expects to take an as-yet undetermined restructuring charge in the quarter in which the transaction closes.
Closing of the deal, which is subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals, is expected during the fourth quarter.
